There has been some extremely fruitful discussion goin on in this thread...and If's journal. I have had many eureka moments in the last few days. So I dug into the charts to apply what I have been learning to the recent PA on E/U.

I saw the QM on the hourly and was so tempted to buy in, but my new understanding of what you guys have been teaching is in its infancy so I just decided to sit and watch. saw Tradingjedi hopped in on it and am very happy for him because he has been working hard and also gives me hope.

Well onto the charts and questions. I have a couple of questions on the charts themselves, but would also like some confirmation on my reading. I was unsure of the lower 1h FTR because price didnt shoot off strong until after a few candles. Now that I think about it, at that time everyone is still trading the trend, so there is going to be more selling from people who waited too long to begin with, which allows for the big boys to load up even more longs. Plus the fact that it never got tested lends to its strength as well.

File to large, had to break it into 2 parts. A question that didnt make it into my second chart, the supply that I have marked in red on the first chart is a RBD/FTR to a FL on the 4h which would indicate major strength and maybe even the ultimate target of the move up. On the other hand it didnt break the most recent lows and retraced to form another ftr that did break the most recent lows and kept going. I am trying to figure out the ultimate target and has it been reached yet. I just took a look at the daily and it is a FL that has been penetrated pretty deeply. So I would say the target has been reached. Still just watching with my new understanding of price.

The concept of price constantly moving from ftr to ftr is slowly coming to me. My charts display the power of FTRs within the current move. Notice the FTRs as price went up got tested and usually produced a newer high, but also consumed the orders there. The ones that didn't produce newer highs after getting tested usually resulted in price moving through the just consumed FTR down to find the next lower untested FTR which then produced a new high. Then when price hit a HTF FTR on the supply side, price went all the way back to the last untested FTR.

What I am working my way through atm is how does price handle opposing FTRs. I am guessing it just knocks price back to the current trends FTR. So what I am thinking is if price just tested that last untested ftr and reacted, then try to find the next opposing FTR and target that, but if there is a key s/r level between that ftr and current price, then price could form a new ftr before it hits the one you found, and then you would want to exit your position. Hope all that makes sense.

My second chart is the 5M from todays action that I really wanted to get it on, but wanted price to test the newly formed FL which it never did. One problem I dont struggle with is chasing price. I have no problem letting price go. In fact I think I may pass on perfectly acceptable entries while practicing "discipline." That is what this next chart is about. Do you guys see a place to get long once you realize price isn't coming back to your entry?

Hope all this is coherent to everyone, I am on my 4th glass of wine and quicly losing the ability to assess myself.

Oh and addressing the current topic of PAZs. I think instead of trying to box price in. We should identify the last key s/r level price just took out and see if price tested and formed an ftr, and then look for the next opposing key s/r level and watch what happens when price gets to it. Does it push through and test and hold above (hold onto position), does it push through and fall back in(fakeout, exit position), or base and retest(form ftr, exit position).

i)yes, you drew it correctly. Also when you see levels stacked like that you should always be aware that price may trade up through the others to get to the last one. You can either hold off on entry till the last one gets hit, or you can split your order up and enter at each level till the turn finally happens. As far as your stop goes I do think you should have put it over that level that turned price, and before the cp because once it hits cp it would probably keep on goin up to the next s/r level.

ii)Not to great at understanding FOs atm. I would get guess FOs are usually done over recent swings (i could definately be wrong here), so I think price's target was just that level.

iii)I can't add anything.

NP man just glad to be helpful. And I agree on the FO, that seems more logical.

Just to clarify. Your stop should not be above the cp. It should be under cp and above the level that got hit. You know that if price is going to turn it will do so at one of those 2 levels. So your stop should not be any higher than just above the levels. Putting it above cp is adding unnecessary risk because you never expect cp to turn price. It would be like putting your stop at the top of a wide range bar.

Keep up the good work.
